beverageMatrices.name: Cold-Pressed Unfiltered Cloudy Apple Cider (pH 3.5, 11.8° Brix, Natural Pectin Cloud)
beverageMatrices.thermalHeatSensitivity: Extremely High (Thermal pasteurization creates cooked applesauce off-flavor and polyphenol browning)
beverageMatrices.description: Freshly pressed cider rich in pectin, suspended pulp particles, and polyphenol oxidase (PPO). The dense CO2 acidification drops micro-environmental pH below 3.0, collapsing guaiacol-producing A. acidoterrestris spores while preserving crisp orchard flavor.

beverageMatrices.name: Freshly Squeezed Valencia Orange Juice (pH 3.7, 12.2° Brix, High Ascorbic Acid)
beverageMatrices.thermalHeatSensitivity: Very High (Thermal flash pasteurization causes cloud precipitation and loss of fresh valencene terpenes)
beverageMatrices.description: High-value citrus juice containing 58 mg/100 mL L-ascorbic acid (Vitamin C). Continuous LT-HPCD inactivates native pectin methylesterase (preventing juice separation) while retaining over 97% of natural vitamin C and fresh aroma volatiles.

beverageMatrices.name: Raw Botanical Probiotic Kombucha & Jasmine Green Tea Infusion (pH 3.1, 5.2° Brix)
beverageMatrices.thermalHeatSensitivity: Critical (Heat pasteurization kills beneficial probiotic symbionts and ruins effervescence)
beverageMatrices.description: Live fermented kombucha with organic gluconic and acetic acids. LT-HPCD selectively eliminates beverage-spoiling wild yeasts and enteric pathogens while simultaneously charging the drink with fine, champagne-like dissolved CO2 micro-bubbles.

beverageMatrices.name: Cold-Brew Craft Coffee Beverage (pH 5.2, 4.8° Brix, Low Acid / High Lipid Matrix)
beverageMatrices.targetPathogen: Clostridium botulinum non-proteolytic spores & Listeria monocytogenes
beverageMatrices.thermalHeatSensitivity: High (Thermal retorting destroys delicate floral coffee aromatics and creates bitter astringency)
beverageMatrices.description: Low-acid specialty coffee beverage requiring stringent pathogen barrier control under FDA refrigerated juice/beverage guidelines. Dense-phase CO2 penetrates bacterial spores without boiling or scorching delicate coffee bean lipids.

beverageMatrices.name: Ultra-Delicate Tender Green Coconut Water (pH 5.0, 5.5° Brix, High Electrolyte & Enzyme Matrix)
beverageMatrices.thermalHeatSensitivity: Extremely Critical (Heat triggers immediate pinking/browning and unpalatable cooked flavor)
beverageMatrices.description: Natural isotonic coconut water packed with potassium and enzymes. Extremely vulnerable to pink discoloration catalyzed by polyphenol oxidase. LT-HPCD halts PPO activity and pasteurizes cold at 20°C with 100% natural color preservation.

beverageMatrices.name: Uncertified Industrial Raw Corn Slurry with Heavy Clostridium Spore Load (Severe Hazard)
beverageMatrices.targetPathogen: Clostridium botulinum proteolytic spores & Bacillus cereus
beverageMatrices.description: CRITICAL HAZARD: Dense raw industrial sweetener carrying massive thermophilic spore counts. High sugar viscosity blocks dense CO2 mass transfer, failing FDA 21 CFR § 120 5-log standards and risking lethal enterotoxin formation.

microbialPathogens.name: Alicyclobacillus acidoterrestris Spores (Thermoacidophilic Spoilage Bacterium)
microbialPathogens.description: The primary threat in pasteurized shelf-stable juices. Produces 2-methoxyphenol (guaiacol), imparting a medicinal disinfectant odor at concentrations as low as 2 ppb. Highly resistant to conventional hot-fill pasteurization but vulnerable to high-pressure CO2 membrane dissolution.

microbialPathogens.name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae & Zygosaccharomyces bailii Spoilage Yeasts
microbialPathogens.description: Common fermentative yeasts causing container swelling, off-gassing, clouding, and package ruptures in unpreserved chilled beverages. Dense CO2 causes massive intracellular acidosis and mechanical cell envelope rupture upon rapid decompression.

microbialPathogens.name: Escherichia coli O157:H7 (Enterohemorrhagic Shiga Toxin-Producing Bacterium)
microbialPathogens.pathogenType: Gram-Negative Enteric Pathogen (FDA Juice HACCP Mandate)
microbialPathogens.description: The statutory pathogen of concern mandated by FDA 21 CFR Part 120 requiring a validated 5-log (100,000-fold) reduction in all commercial fruit and vegetable juices. Readily eradicated by dense CO2 intracellular acidification.

microbialPathogens.name: Salmonella enterica (Serovars Typhimurium, Enteritidis, Newport)
microbialPathogens.description: Major cause of foodborne outbreaks associated with unpasteurized orange juice and apple cider. Inactivated rapidly under dense-phase CO2 as lipophilic CO2 molecules strip outer membrane lipopolysaccharides.

microbialPathogens.name: Listeria monocytogenes (Psychrotrophic Listeriosis Pathogen)
microbialPathogens.description: Dangerous pathogen capable of multiplying at refrigerated temperatures (4°C) with mortality rates up to 20–30% in vulnerable populations. Effectively eliminated by high-pressure CO2 through membrane lipid extraction.

co2DosingMechanisms.name: Sintered Porous Titanium Micro-Bubble Injection Sparger (5 µm Pore Core)
co2DosingMechanisms.description: Produces millions of dense-phase CO2 micro-bubbles per milliliter, maximizing interfacial contact area and dissolving carbon dioxide into the juice stream within fractions of a second according to Henry's law.

co2DosingMechanisms.name: Sulzer SMX Plus Cross-Bar High-Shear Static Contactor Manifold
co2DosingMechanisms.description: Forces the co-injected high-pressure liquid juice and dense CO2 through cross-bar element grids, generating shear rates up to 35,000 s^-1 to break interfacial boundaries and ensure homogeneous dissolution.

co2DosingMechanisms.name: Venturi Hydrodynamic High-Pressure Cavitating Injector
co2DosingMechanisms.description: Accelerates the beverage through a converging-diverging venturi nozzle, creating localized pressure drops that aspirate dense CO2 and generate micro-cavitation shocks that assist in microbial cell wall weakening.

co2DosingMechanisms.name: Defective Open Bypass Pipe without Micro-Sparger (Severe Stratification Hazard)
co2DosingMechanisms.description: CRITICAL PROCESS FAILURE: Gas flows along the top of the conduit while liquid flows beneath with near-zero interfacial dissolution. Results in complete failure to achieve 5-log microbial reduction.

decompressionNozzleTypes.name: Servo-Controlled Silicon Carbide (SiC) Ceramic Micro-Orifice Nozzle
decompressionNozzleTypes.erosionResistance: Superior (Zero dimensional loss after 8,000 operating hours)
decompressionNozzleTypes.description: High-hardness ceramic orifice capable of withstanding supersonic decompression velocities without abrasive wear from beverage particulates, maintaining ultra-fine dissolved CO2 effervescence.

decompressionNozzleTypes.name: Coaxial Induction-Heated Decompression Expansion Nozzle
decompressionNozzleTypes.erosionResistance: High (AISI 316L with DLC Diamond-Like Carbon Coating)
decompressionNozzleTypes.description: Integrated high-frequency induction heating prevents Joule-Thomson freeze-choking and dry ice crystal packing during high-pressure gas expansion, ensuring continuous 24/7 unhindered flow.

decompressionNozzleTypes.name: Multi-Stage Tortuous Path Sanitary Labyrinth Pressure-Letdown Valve
decompressionNozzleTypes.erosionResistance: Very High (Stellite Trim and Hastelloy C Plugs)
decompressionNozzleTypes.description: Stepwise pressure reduction designed specifically for sparkling beverages and sodas, minimizing shear-induced gas breakout and maximizing dissolved carbonation stability in the finished bottle.

carbonationSaturationProfiles.targetBeverages: Craft sodas, probiotic kombuchas, sparkling lemonades, ginger beers

regulatoryStandards.standard: FDA 21 CFR Part 120 (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point Systems for Juice)
regulatoryStandards.requirement: Mandates that commercial processors apply treatments that achieve a minimum 5-log (100,000-fold) reduction in the pertinent microorganism of public health significance (e.g., E. coli O157:H7 or Salmonella enterica) in juice.
regulatoryStandards.status: Full Compliance (LT-HPCD achieves 6.5+ log reduction at 120+ bar / 25°C without thermal degradation)

regulatoryStandards.standard: FDA 21 CFR § 184.1240 (Direct Food Substances Affirmed as Generally Recognized as Safe - Carbon Dioxide)
regulatoryStandards.requirement: Affirms food-grade carbon dioxide as GRAS for use as an antimicrobial agent, carbonating agent, and processing aid with no toxic solvent residues.
regulatoryStandards.status: Certified Food-Grade (Purity ≥ 99.95%, conforming to CGA G-6.2 beverage grade standards)

regulatoryStandards.standard: ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code (BPVC) Section VIII Divisions 1 & 2
regulatoryStandards.requirement: Requires robust pressure vessel calculations, 4:1 burst safety factor, full volumetric radiograph inspection of welded joints, and ASME UV-stamped safety pressure relief valves for systems operating above 15 psig (1.03 bar).
regulatoryStandards.status: Stamped & Certified (Design pressure 250 bar, operating limit 150 bar, dual redundant rupture discs)

regulatoryStandards.standard: 3-A Sanitary Standards 60-01 (Pumps) & 61-01 (High Pressure Homogenizers & In-Line Contactors)
regulatoryStandards.requirement: Demands all product-contact surfaces have an electropolished surface roughness Ra ≤ 0.38 µm (15 µin), self-draining sanitary geometries, and complete Clean-in-Place (CIP) cleanability.
regulatoryStandards.status: Fully Certified (AISI 316L / Hastelloy C-22 wetted components with Kalrez 6230 FDA-compliant elastomers)

regulatoryStandards.standard: Compressed Gas Association (CGA) G-6.2 Specification for Beverage-Grade Carbon Dioxide
regulatoryStandards.requirement: Sets strict limits on impurities in carbon dioxide used in foods and beverages: moisture < 20 ppm, total hydrocarbons < 50 ppm, benzene < 0.02 ppm, and total sulfur < 0.1 ppm.
regulatoryStandards.status: Strictly Monitored (Continuous in-line spectroscopic impurity validation before high-pressure dosing)

regulatoryStandards.standard: European Hygienic Engineering & Design Group (EHEDG) Guidelines Doc 8 & Doc 16
regulatoryStandards.requirement: Specifies aseptic sealing criteria, bacteria-tight elastomer grooves, avoidance of dead legs (L/D < 1.5), and in-line steam sterilization (SIP) compatibility.
regulatoryStandards.status: Class I Aseptic Certified (Zero dead legs, automated CIP caustic/acid sanitization protocol)
